items.title: Weak topology on a normed space
items.statement: For a real or complex normed space X, sigma(X,X*) is the initial topology induced by its bounded scalar-linear functionals.
items.strategy: Use scalar-linear duals throughout; convexity is real convexity and separation uses real parts in the complex case.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Basic weak neighborhoods
items.statement: At x, sets defined by finitely many inequalities |f_j(y-x)|<epsilon, with epsilon>0 and f_j in X*, form a weak neighborhood base.
items.strategy: Intersect finitely many inverse images of scalar open disks; shrink their radii to one positive minimum. Show vector addition and scalar multiplication are continuous and these neighborhoods are convex and balanced at zero.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Weak topology is hausdorff
items.statement: Assume HB. The weak topology of a real or complex normed space is Hausdorff.
items.strategy: For x!=y use relative Hahn-Banach dual norming to choose a bounded functional separating them, then take disjoint scalar disks. This uses HB only through the relative norming corollary, not the full-Axiom-of-Choice Hahn-Banach implementation.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Weak convergence of nets and sequences
items.statement: A net x_i converges weakly to x when f(x_i) tends to f(x) for every f in X*. Sequences are the special case indexed by the natural numbers.
items.strategy: Finite simultaneous eventual conditions are exactly the neighborhood definition of convergence. Closure is topological, never defined by sequences.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Basic weak star neighborhoods
items.statement: At f in X*, finite inequalities |(g-f)(x_j)|<epsilon form a weak-star neighborhood base.
items.strategy: Use the predecessor initial topology on evaluations. Evaluations distinguish distinct functionals, so this topology is Hausdorff in ZF without norming HB. Verify vector operations and local convexity directly.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Weak star convergence
items.statement: A net f_i in X* converges weak-star to f in X* exactly when f_i(x) tends to f(x) for every x in X.
items.strategy: The specified limit must belong to X*: pointwise limits of bounded functionals on an incomplete space need not be bounded.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Continuous dual of a weak topology
items.statement: The scalar-linear continuous dual of (X,sigma(X,X*)) is X*.
items.strategy: Continuity at zero bounds a functional on a finite-coordinate neighborhood. Scaling proves it vanishes on the common kernel; factor through the image in the finite-dimensional coordinate space, extend there using a finite basis, and express it as a finite linear combination of the original functionals. No algebraic-dual identification.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Continuous dual of a weak star topology
items.statement: Assume HB. Every weak-star continuous scalar-linear functional on X* is f -> f(x) for a unique x in X.
items.strategy: Factor through finitely many evaluations using their common kernel and finite-dimensional extension. Their linear combination is evaluation at a single vector. Existence is in ZF; uniqueness uses point separation from the relative Hahn-Banach norming corollary.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Norm closed convex iff weakly closed
items.statement: Assume HB. A convex subset of a normed space is norm closed iff it is weakly closed. More generally its norm and weak closures agree.
items.strategy: Weak-open sets are norm open. If x is outside the norm closure, apply relative geometric Hahn-Banach to the closed convex norm closure and the singleton {x}; the separating functional gives a weak neighborhood of x missing the set. Use real parts in the complex case.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Weak closure of the unit sphere is the closed unit ball
items.statement: Assume HB. In an infinite-dimensional normed space, the weak closure of the norm unit sphere is the closed unit ball.
items.strategy: Given x of norm<1 and finitely many tests, finite-dimensional rank gives a nonzero vector in their common kernel. Along its real line through x, continuity of the norm and the intermediate value theorem give a point of norm one in the prescribed weak neighborhood. The reverse inclusion follows from the preceding HB-relative weak closedness of the ball.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Weakly convergent sequences are norm bounded
items.statement: Assuming the norming Hahn–Banach principle and countable choice, every weakly convergent sequence in a normed space is norm bounded; if X is Banach, every weak-star convergent sequence in X* is norm bounded.
items.strategy: Apply the AC_omega sequential uniform-boundedness theorem to J_X(x_n) on the Banach space X*, then use the HB-relative bidual isometry. For weak-star convergent sequences apply sequential uniform boundedness directly on the assumed Banach space X. No DC or full AC is used.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Weak convergence implies lower semicontinuity of the norm
items.statement: Assume HB. For a weakly convergent net x_i -> x, ||x|| <= liminf_i ||x_i|| (extended-real net liminf).
items.strategy: For each unit-dual f, |f(x)|=lim |f(x_i)| <= liminf ||x_i||; use the HB-relative dual norm formula. Equivalently, apply weak closedness of every closed norm ball. No boundedness of the net is asserted.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Weak and norm topologies agree iff finite dimensional
items.statement: The weak and norm topologies agree exactly when X is finite dimensional.
items.strategy: Coordinate functionals in finite dimension give the norm topology. In infinite dimension every finite family has a nonzero common kernel, so every weak neighborhood of zero is norm unbounded.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Infinite dimensional weak topology is not first countable
items.statement: Assume HB and countable choice. An infinite-dimensional normed space has no countable weak local base at zero.
items.strategy: Use AC_omega once to refine each member of a supplied countable local base by a finite-coordinate basic neighborhood; the countable union of those finite lists enumerates a spanning set for X* by finite-coordinate factorization. Deterministic greedy extraction yields a finite or countably infinite Hamel basis. The dual X* is Banach and the latter case is excluded in ZF by the no-countably-infinite-Hamel-basis theorem. In the finite case, HB-relative separation forces X finite-dimensional, a contradiction. No DC or full AC is used.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Annihilators are weak and weak star closed
items.statement: For M subset X and N subset X*, M-perp is weak-star closed and preannihilator N is weakly closed in ZF. Assuming HB, the earlier bipolar identities for linear subspaces apply.
items.strategy: Intersect the appropriate evaluation kernels for the choice-free closedness assertions. For the primal closure identity use HB-relative geometric separation; cite the published weak-star bipolar theorem at its original home for the dual identity, without duplicating or rehoming it.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Transpose is weak to weak continuous
items.statement: A bounded T:X->Y is weak-to-weak continuous; its transpose T*:Y*->X* is continuous for the weak topologies sigma(Y*,Y**) and sigma(X*,X**).
items.strategy: For T compose each y* with T. Apply the same reasoning to the bounded operator T*, testing by X**.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Transpose is weak star to weak star continuous
items.statement: Assume HB. A bounded T:X->Y has weak-star continuous transpose T*:Y*->X*. Conversely a bounded weak-star continuous scalar-linear S:Y*->X* has a unique bounded preadjoint T:X->Y with S=T*.
items.strategy: For each x, f -> (Sf)(x) is weak-star continuous and hence evaluation at a unique Tx by the preceding HB-relative dual identification. Uniqueness proves linearity; HB-relative dual norming gives ||Tx||=sup_{||f||<=1}|(Sf)(x)|<=||S||||x||. Thus T is bounded, and the defining equality gives S=T*. Conversely, composition gives ||T*f||<=||T||||f|| and evaluation makes T* weak-star continuous. Do not appeal to the published transpose norm-equality lemma, whose norming-functional dependency has an undeclared HB assumption; equality of norms is not needed here. Do not require reflexivity or completeness.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Strong and weak operator topologies
items.statement: On B(X,Y), SOT is initial for T->Tx with Y norm topology; WOT is initial for T->f(Tx), x in X, f in Y*.
items.strategy: Specify nets: strong convergence means ||T_i x-Tx||->0 for each x; weak operator convergence means f(T_i x)->f(Tx) for each x,f.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Norm implies strong implies weak operator convergence
items.statement: For nets of bounded operators, norm convergence implies SOT convergence, which implies WOT convergence.
items.strategy: Use ||(T_i-T)x||<=||T_i-T||||x|| and |f((T_i-T)x)|<=||f||||(T_i-T)x||. No assertion that reverse implications hold.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

title: Weak and Weak Star Topologies — Examples

items.title: Coordinate vectors converge weakly to zero in ell p
items.statement: In real or complex ell^p, 1<p<infinity, e_n tends weakly to zero while ||e_n||=1.
items.strategy: For a bounded functional F set b_n=F(e_n). On every finite initial segment, test F against the phase-adjusted sequence with coordinates |b_n|^(q-1); boundedness and the finite Holder/power identities give a uniform bound on the partial sums of |b_n|^q. Hence b is in ell^q and in particular b_n tends to zero. This argument works directly over the reals and complexes, uses only finite choices and monotone real-series limits, and avoids the published real-only ell-p duality corollary with its undeclared AC dependency. Finally F(e_n)=b_n and ||e_n||=1.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Coordinate vectors do not converge weakly to zero in ell one
items.statement: In real or complex ell^1 the coordinate vectors do not converge weakly to zero.
items.strategy: Define the summation functional directly over either scalar field. Absolute convergence gives |sum x_n|<=||x||_1, so it is bounded and has value 1 at every e_n. Coordinate-evaluation functionals force any weak limit to have every coordinate zero, while the summation functional excludes convergence to zero. This proof does not need a dual-representation theorem.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Coordinate evaluations converge weak star to zero in ell one star
items.statement: Over the real or complex scalars, the coordinate functionals e_n in ell^infinity=(ell^1)* converge weak-star to zero and all have norm 1.
items.strategy: The complex dual identification is published. For real scalars, repeat its direct coefficient proof: bounded sequences define bounded summation pairings, every functional's coefficients are bounded, and finite truncations recover the functional; no choice is used. Every absolutely summable x has x_n->0, which is exactly weak-star convergence of the coordinate functionals, and testing the coordinate vectors gives norm one.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Weak star and weak topologies on a dual can differ
items.statement: On ell^1=(c0)*, weak-star and weak topologies differ.
items.strategy: e_n is weak-star null since every x in c0 has x_n->0. The bounded summation functional on ell^1 equals 1 on e_n, so the sequence is not weakly null.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Weak closure can exceed sequential weak closure
items.statement: Assume HB and the Axiom of Countable Choice. In real ell^2 the set A={sqrt(n)e_n:n>=1} is sequentially weakly closed, but zero belongs to its weak closure and not to A.
items.strategy: For each bounded F on real ell^2, the finite-vector test x_N=sum_{n<N}F(e_n)e_n and boundedness give sum_{n<N}|F(e_n)|^2<=||F||^2, so the coefficient sequence lies in ell^2; continuity and convergence of finite truncations give F(x)=sum x_nF(e_n). Thus, if finitely many tests exclude every sqrt(n)e_n from a basic zero-neighborhood, summing their coefficient squares would dominate a constant multiple of the divergent harmonic series, a contradiction. Any weakly convergent sequence in A is norm bounded by the preceding HB+AC_omega theorem, hence has finite range; weak Hausdorffness under HB makes that finite set closed and puts the limit in A. HB and AC_omega are used only through those two preceding weak-topology results; the ell^2 coefficient argument is choice-free and avoids the defective published duality corollary.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Right shift powers converge in wot not sot
items.statement: On real or complex ell^2 the powers R^n of the unilateral right shift converge in WOT to zero but not in SOT.
items.strategy: For a bounded real or complex functional F, finite phase-adjusted tests give sum_{k<N}|F(e_k)|^2<=||F||^2; finite truncations then show F(x)=sum_k x_kF(e_k). Cauchy–Schwarz bounds F(R^n x) by ||x|| times the ell^2 tail norm of the coefficient sequence, which tends to zero. Since every R^n is an isometry, the powers do not converge strongly. The coefficient proof is inline and choice-free, avoiding the published real-only ell-p duality corollary and its undeclared AC dependency.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Left shift powers converge in sot not operator norm
items.statement: On ell^2 the powers L^n of the unilateral left shift converge in SOT to zero but ||L^n||=1.
items.strategy: The squared norm is the tail sum of |x_k|^2. The moving witness e_(n+1) proves the lower operator norm bound. No Hilbert adjoint theorem is used.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Pointwise boundedness without a uniform bound on an incomplete domain
items.statement: On c00 with the supremum norm, T_n(x)=n x_n is pointwise eventually zero, but ||T_n||=n. The domain is incomplete.
items.strategy: Finite support gives eventual zero, and e_n attains the norm bound. Finite truncations of (1/k) are Cauchy in the supremum norm and their only possible coordinatewise limit is not in c00. Reprove directly rather than using a foreign B item as a dependency.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: A weakly convergent net need not be eventually norm bounded
items.statement: Every infinite-dimensional normed space has a weakly null net whose norms tend to infinity.
items.strategy: Index by all triples (U,n,x) with U a weak zero-neighborhood, n a positive integer, x in U and ||x||>=n. Order by reverse inclusion of U and increasing n; ties give a directed preorder. Nonempty finite intersections are unbounded by the kernel argument. The net is the carried point x. This avoids choosing a point for every neighborhood globally; it is not eventually norm bounded.

references.title: Bühler–Salamon, Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage
Teschl, Topics in Real and Functional Analysis (2017); exact harvest in batch coverage

items.title: Test function space d of an open set
items.strategy: Use the existing real multi-index convention componentwise for complex-valued tests; compact supports are contained in Omega.
items.statement: D(Omega)=C_c^infinity(Omega;C), Omega open in R^n, n>=1. Pairings are complex bilinear, with no conjugation.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Fixed support test function frechet space
items.strategy: Define the seminorm topology and displayed metric; completeness is proved in the following lemma rather than assumed from the name Frechet.
items.statement: D_K consists of tests supported in K compactly contained in Omega, with p_m=max_{|alpha|<=m} sup_K |partial^alpha phi|.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Test function topology
items.strategy: Define through the family of seminorms continuous on every D_K; the universal-property lemma proves existence and the topology claims. Do not define it by sequences.
items.statement: D carries the finest locally convex topology making each D_K inclusion continuous.

references.title: Razvan Gelca, Functional Analysis

items.title: Distribution
items.strategy: Use actual LF continuity, not an unsupported sequence-only definition.
items.statement: A distribution is a continuous complex-linear functional D(Omega)->C.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Regular distribution from a locally integrable function
items.strategy: Absolute integrability holds on each compact support; continuity and injectivity are next.
items.statement: For f locally integrable, u_f(phi)=integral f phi.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Convolution of a distribution with a test function
items.strategy: Reflection accounts for signs; smoothness and continuity are proved next.
items.statement: On R^n set (u*phi)(x)=<u(y),phi(x-y)> for phi in D. On Omega use only x for which x-supp(phi) is contained in Omega.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Test function cutoffs and euclidean localization
items.statement: In ZF, for compact K in an open Euclidean set Omega, construct chi in C_c^infinity(Omega), 0<=chi<=1, equal to one on a neighborhood of K. Every open cover of Omega has a countable locally finite smooth subordinate partition with compact supports.
items.strategy: Translate and rescale the earlier explicit smooth-step cutoff to finitely many balls covering K, combine them by 1-product(1-chi_j), and keep the finite support margin inside Omega. For an open cover, enumerate all rational balls whose closures are compactly contained in some cover member; no cover member need be selected because subordination asks only for its existence. Use the fixed distance-to-boundary exhaustion and lexicographically least finite subcovers on successive shells, obtain a deterministic locally finite family of rescaled explicit bumps, and normalize its positive sum. Supply every support and local-finiteness margin. This is a ZF construction and uses neither mollification nor the later manifold page.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Fixed support test function spaces are complete
items.statement: D_K is complete for d(f,g)=sum 2^(-m) min(1,p_m(f-g)). Its topology is the derivative-seminorm topology.
items.strategy: Take uniform limits of each derivative on all of R^n after zero extension. Integrating along coordinate segments identifies successive derivatives; all limits vanish outside K. This also handles compact K with empty interior.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Test function lf topology universal property
items.statement: The locally convex final topology exists, is Hausdorff, induces the prescribed topology on every D_K, is independent of compact exhaustion, and a linear map to a locally convex space is continuous iff each restriction to D_K is continuous.
items.strategy: Use all seminorms whose restrictions to each D_K are continuous. Global derivative sup seminorms separate points and recover the topology on each D_K. A seminorm composed with a candidate linear map proves the universal property; cofinality proves exhaustion independence. Prove continuity of vector operations directly from seminorm balls.

references.title: Razvan Gelca, Functional Analysis

items.title: Test function operations are continuous
items.strategy: Control supports under each map and bound each derivative seminorm by finitely many source seminorms using chain and Leibniz rules. Treat parameter-dependent translation separately in the parameter lemma.
items.statement: Differentiation, multiplication by fixed a in C^infinity, translations between translated domains, and composition by a diffeomorphism are continuous on test spaces.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Local finite order characterization of distributions
items.strategy: Continuity on each seminorm space gives a finite intersection of neighborhoods; scale to a bound. Apply the LF universal property for the converse.
items.statement: u is a distribution iff for each compact K there are C_K and m_K with |u(phi)|<=C_K p_{m_K}(phi) on D_K.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Order of a distribution on a compact set
items.strategy: Separate compactwise order from the uniform order exponent. Arbitrary distributions may have unbounded orders along an exhaustion.
items.statement: Order on K is the least m with a bound on D_K (zero distribution assigned order 0); global finite order means one m works for every K, while constants may vary.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Distributional derivative
items.strategy: Continuous transpose of differentiation defines a distribution.
items.statement: partial^alpha u(phi)=(-1)^|alpha| u(partial^alpha phi).

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Multiplication of a distribution by a smooth function
items.strategy: Use continuity of test multiplication; no product of arbitrary distributions is introduced.
items.statement: a u(phi)=u(a phi) for a smooth.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Leibniz rule for distributions
items.strategy: Prove first-order identity by testing and subtracting the derivative on a; iterate by the binomial recurrence.
items.statement: partial^alpha(a u)=sum_{beta<=alpha} binom(alpha,beta) (partial^beta a) partial^(alpha-beta)u.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Dirac delta and its derivatives
items.strategy: Evaluation and its derivatives obey fixed-support finite-order estimates.
items.statement: delta_a(phi)=phi(a); partial^alpha delta_a(phi)=(-1)^|alpha| partial^alpha phi(a).

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Distributions form a sheaf
items.strategy: Restrictions use zero extension of tests. Define the glued value using a locally finite smooth partition; on any compact only finitely many summands occur, so continuity follows from finitely many finite-order bounds. Use refinements to establish independence.
items.statement: Compatible distributions on an arbitrary open cover glue uniquely.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Support of a distribution
items.strategy: The sheaf locality result proves the union of vanishing opens is itself a vanishing open. A test vanishing near support pairs to zero.
items.statement: Support is the complement of the largest open subset on which u vanishes.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Compactly supported distributions have global finite order
items.strategy: Insert chi=1 near support, apply the D_L estimate, and expand derivatives of chi phi. The bound concerns a compact neighborhood, not just the support itself.
items.statement: A compactly supported distribution admits |u(phi)|<=C max_{|alpha|<=m} sup_L |partial^alpha phi| for every test phi, with one compact neighborhood L of its support.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Distributions supported at one point
items.strategy: Taylor remainder and shrinking cutoffs show u kills every test whose finite jet at a vanishes. Factor through the finite jet space, and use cutoff monomials to identify coefficients. The zero combination has empty support, so do not assert support equals {a} without nonzero hypothesis.
items.statement: If supp(u) subset {a}, then u is a finite linear combination of derivatives of delta_a; conversely such combinations have support contained in {a}.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Bounded test function sets have common compact support
items.statement: B is bounded in D iff all its supports lie in a single compact K and sup_{f in B} p_m(f)<infinity for every m. Bounded means absorbed by every zero neighborhood.
items.strategy: Use a fixed compact exhaustion. If no K contains all supports, define from B itself (without selecting witnesses) an increasing sequence of least occupied shells and, on each such shell, the extended-real supremum A_j of |f(x)| over f in B. Assign that shell a finite weight j/A_j when 0<A_j<infinity and weight 1 when A_j=infinity, interpolate to a locally bounded continuous weight w, and set q(f)=sup_x w(x)|f(x)|. Its restriction to each D_K is continuous, while sup_{f in B}q(f) is infinite, contradicting boundedness. Thus all supports lie in one K; the global derivative seminorms then give the derivative bounds. Conversely those bounds absorb B in every continuous-seminorm neighborhood. This aggregate-supremum construction is in ZF and makes no countable selection. Convergent sequences plus their limits are bounded by finite-tail absorption.

references.title: Razvan Gelca, Functional Analysis

items.title: Sequential convergence in test function space
items.strategy: Convergent sequences are bounded, hence have common compact support; use the induced D_K topology. Conversely the continuous inclusion carries D_K convergence to D.
items.statement: phi_j->phi in D iff the supports eventually lie in one compact K and every derivative converges uniformly.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Weak and strong topologies on distributions
items.strategy: Finite-order estimates and the bounded-set lemma show each strong seminorm is finite. Distinguish nets from sequences.
items.statement: Weak topology is generated by |u(phi)|; strong topology by sup_{phi in B}|u(phi)| for bounded B in D.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Locally integrable functions embed in distributions
items.strategy: Bound by ||f||_{L1(K)} p_0(phi). If all pairings vanish, local mollifications vanish; multiply by a cutoff and apply L1 approximate identities to obtain f=0 a.e. Bounded test sets give the continuity assertion.
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. The map L1_loc(Omega)/a.e. -> D prime is injective and continuous for local L1 and strong distribution topologies.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Strong distribution convergence implies weak convergence
items.strategy: Every singleton test set is bounded. No unrestricted converse for nets is asserted.
items.statement: Strong convergence implies weak convergence.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Distributional differentiation is continuous and commutes
items.strategy: Commuting smooth partials gives commutation; integration by parts gives agreement. A continuous linear map sends bounded sets to bounded sets, so transpose continuity holds strongly as well as weakly.
items.statement: Distribution derivatives commute, extend classical derivatives, and are continuous in both weak and strong dual topologies.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Distribution pairing with smooth parameter families
items.statement: If F(x,y) is smooth and its y-support stays in a common compact set as x ranges over a compact subset, then x -> u(F(x,.)) is smooth and derivatives pass through u. Compact parameter integrals commute with u.
items.strategy: Taylor remainder estimates in every fixed-support seminorm give convergence of difference quotients; continuous functionals preserve those limits. Approximate compact integrals by Riemann sums in D_K, with all derivative errors controlled.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Convolution with a test function is smooth
items.strategy: On compact x-sets the y-tests have common compact support; apply the parameter lemma. The sign from reflection cancels the distribution derivative sign.
items.statement: u*phi is smooth on its domain and partial^alpha(u*phi)=(partial^alpha u)*phi=u*(partial^alpha phi).

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Uniform finite order bounds for pointwise bounded distributions
items.statement: Assume DC. A pointwise bounded family of distributions has a common finite-order estimate on each D_K; every pointwise limit of distributions is a distribution.
items.strategy: Apply complete-metric Baire on D_K to the closed sets where every functional has modulus at most j. Subtract a ball from itself and scale to obtain the common seminorm estimate. Uses DC through Baire, not merely the normed-space uniform boundedness theorem.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Pullback of a distribution by a diffeomorphism
items.statement: For a smooth diffeomorphism F:U->V define <F^*u,phi>=<u,(phi/|det DF|) composed with F^{-1}>. Test functions use composition; distributions use the absolute Jacobian. Assuming the Axiom of Countable Choice, regular distributions satisfy F^*u_f=u_{f composed with F}.
items.strategy: The definition and its continuity are choice-free: support maps to a compact subset of V and all derivative seminorms obey chain/product estimates. Under AC_omega, verify F^*u_f=u_{f composed with F} by the published L1 change-of-variables formula, whose completion step is the exact use of AC_omega. Do not define pullback by arbitrary smooth maps.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Tensor product of distributions
items.statement: <u tensor v,Phi>=<u(x),<v(y),Phi(x,y)>> for compactly supported smooth Phi on U times V.
items.strategy: Parameter pairing gives a compactly supported smooth outer test function. This defines the candidate; continuity and pairing-order independence are established next.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Compactly supported distributions extend to smooth functions
items.statement: For compactly supported u, <u,f>=<u,chi f> defines a unique continuous extension to C^infinity, independent of chi=1 near supp(u).
items.strategy: The difference of two cutoff tests vanishes near the support; locality kills it. The finite-order bound gives continuity. Cutoff exhaustion converges in C^infinity, proving uniqueness without Hahn-Banach.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Sequential convergence of smooth multipliers and distributions
items.statement: Assume DC. If u_j->u weakly in D prime and a_j->a in C infinity on compact sets, then a_j u_j->a u weakly.
items.strategy: For a fixed test phi, all a_j phi lie in D_K and converge there; the DC-dependent common finite-order bound for u_j controls u_j((a_j-a)phi), and weak convergence controls (u_j-u)(a phi). DC is used only through the preceding Baire argument.

references.title: Razvan Gelca, Functional Analysis

items.title: Extension by zero for distributions with ambient closed support
items.statement: If F is closed in R^n, F subset Omega open, and u in D prime(Omega) has support contained in F, then u extends uniquely to a distribution on R^n with support contained in F.
items.strategy: Glue u on Omega and zero on R^n minus F. They agree on the overlap. Ambient closedness is essential; do not promise extension across boundary for arbitrary distributions.

references.title: Razvan Gelca, Functional Analysis

items.title: Translation invariant test function operators are convolutions
items.statement: A continuous linear map L:D(R^n)->C(R^n), with the compact-open topology on C, commuting with translations is convolution by a unique distribution. Its outputs are smooth.
items.strategy: Define u(phi)=(L(check phi))(0), which is continuous. Translation invariance gives Lphi(x)=u(phi(x-.)); smoothness follows from the convolution theorem. Conversely finite-order parameter estimates show u convolution is continuous D->C infinity.

references.title: Razvan Gelca, Functional Analysis

items.title: Complex l one functionals on finite measure spaces have bounded densities
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. A bounded complex-linear functional on complex L1 of a finite-measure space has a bounded complex density g representing it by integral f g.
items.strategy: Apply the AC-explicit finite-measure real p=1 Radon-Nikodym representation lemma to the real and imaginary parts of the functional restricted to real functions, obtaining integrable real densities. For either density h, test on indicators of the level sets {h>M} and {h<-M}: boundedness of the functional forces those sets to be null for every rational M above its norm, hence h is essentially bounded. Combine the two real densities and extend the identity by complex linearity; twice the original operator norm is a sufficient bound. AC is used exactly through the real Radon-Nikodym representation lemma, and boundedness is proved here rather than attributed to that lemma.

references.title: Razvan Gelca, Functional Analysis; complete Chapter 7 reading recorded in batch coverage

items.title: Local structure of distributions as derivatives of continuous functions
items.strategy: Localize by a cutoff first and extend the compactly supported distribution to R^n; enclose its support in a box. Iterated FTC bounds p_m(phi) by C||partial_1^(m+1)...partial_n^(m+1)phi||_1. HB extends the induced functional on that derivative image by the relative complex norm-preserving theorem. AC is used by the finite-measure L1 density lemma. Integrate the bounded density once in each coordinate to obtain a continuous function whose regular distribution has the required mixed derivative. Do not assume arbitrary K itself is a cube.
items.statement: Assume HB and the Axiom of Choice. For each K compactly contained in Omega, u agrees on D_K with one finite mixed derivative of a continuous function on Omega.

references.title: Razvan Gelca, Functional Analysis

items.title: Compact support continuous primitive representation
items.statement: Assume HB and the Axiom of Choice. If u has compact support K and order m, for K subset V open there are finitely many continuous g_beta supported in V with u=sum partial^beta g_beta; beta_j<=m+2 is sufficient.
items.strategy: Use a cutoff supported in a relatively compact neighborhood inside V; the local HB-and-AC primitive representation and Leibniz expansion produce continuous coefficient functions with the required supports. No further choice is used.

references.title: Razvan Gelca, Functional Analysis

items.title: Global locally finite structure of distributions
items.strategy: Localize by the deterministic countable locally finite compact partition, use AC to select one support-controlled primitive representation for each localized distribution, and group equal multi-indices. Each compact meets finitely many local pieces and therefore finitely many orders. Uniform order bounds give one finite multi-index box. HB and AC also enter through the local representation theorem.
items.statement: Assume HB and the Axiom of Choice. Every distribution is a locally finite sum sum_alpha partial^alpha u_{g_alpha} of continuous functions; if its global order is finite, only finitely many multi-indices are needed.

references.title: Razvan Gelca, Functional Analysis

items.title: Finite sums of product tests are dense on product open sets
items.statement: Every test on U times V is a D-limit of finite sums f_j(x)g_j(y), with all supports in one compact product.
items.strategy: Convolve with product unit-mass mollifiers of small radius; all derivatives converge uniformly with one compact support margin. Approximate the parameter integral by finite Riemann sums of separated kernels in every derivative seminorm. Diagonal choices give convergence in D. No distribution convolution or Fourier-series theorem is required.

references.title: Razvan Gelca, Functional Analysis; complete Chapter 7 reading recorded in batch coverage

items.title: Tensor product distributions and iterated pairings
items.statement: The tensor pairing is a distribution, has support supp(u) times supp(v), and is unchanged on exchanging the order of the pairings. Three-factor pairings associate.
items.strategy: Prove a mixed-derivative estimate on each product compact. Iterated pairings agree on separated tests; apply the product-test density lemma to pass to every test. Repeat in three blocks. Locality and products of local witnesses identify tensor support.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Convolution of distributions when one has compact support
items.strategy: Choose a cutoff equal to one near (supp u times supp v) intersect addition^{-1}(supp psi), which is compact under the stated support hypothesis.
items.statement: If at least one of u,v has compact support on R^n, define u*v on a test psi by the tensor pairing with a compact cutoff times psi(x+y).

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Convolution of distributions is well defined under the support hypothesis
items.strategy: Compactness of the relevant intersection allows one cutoff per compact family of tests. Tensor support kills the cutoff difference; mixed derivative bounds give continuity. Closedness of the sum uses one compact summand.
items.statement: The convolution candidate is cutoff-independent, continuous on each D_K, commutative, and has support contained in supp(u)+supp(v).

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Mollifier approximation in distributions
items.strategy: Test using reflected mollifier convolution. Supports stay in one compact neighborhood and all derivatives converge uniformly. For a global smooth approximating sequence use cutoffs along an exhaustion before mollifying.
items.statement: For u in D prime(Omega), local convolution with rho_epsilon converges weakly to u as epsilon tends to zero.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: A distribution with zero derivatives on a connected open set is constant
items.strategy: Mollify on relatively compact balls: derivatives of the smooth mollifications vanish. Their constants converge by testing against a fixed unit-integral test. Pass to u and glue constants across overlapping balls using connectedness.
items.statement: If all first derivatives of u vanish on a connected nonempty open set, u equals one constant regular distribution; on a disconnected set constants may differ by component.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Smooth functions are weakly dense in distributions
items.strategy: Use exhaustion cutoffs chi_j equal to one on increasing compacts and radii epsilon_j tending to zero so chi_j u can be extended by zero and convolved globally. On any fixed compact the argument eventually reduces to the mollifier theorem.
items.statement: Smooth regular distributions are weakly dense in D prime(Omega).

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Associativity of distribution convolution under compact support
items.strategy: Use a common compact cutoff in the three-variable pairing on each test support. Tensor pairing independence proves associativity; differentiation passes under pairing. Do not claim arbitrary pairwise existence guarantees associativity. A stronger properly-summing triple statement needs its explicit properness proof.
items.statement: For u,v,w with at least two compactly supported, (u*v)*w=u*(v*w); derivatives commute with permitted convolution. Also delta_0*u=u and (partial^alpha delta_0)*u=partial^alpha u.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Closed bounded test function sets are compact
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice and DC. Every closed bounded subset of D(Omega) is compact.
items.strategy: Locate it in D_K; bounds on next derivatives give equicontinuity on a containing box after zero extension. Apply the AC_omega-and-DC real Arzela-Ascoli theorem separately to real and imaginary parts of every derivative, take the explicitly countable diagonal, and use derivative compatibility. Metric compactness in D_K and the continuous inclusion give compactness in D. The stated choice principles are used exactly through Arzela-Ascoli and metric compactness.

references.title: Razvan Gelca, Functional Analysis; complete Chapter 7 reading recorded in batch coverage

title: Distributions Test Functions and Differentiation — Examples

items.title: Derivative of the heaviside function is dirac delta
items.strategy: Integrate -integral_0^infinity phi prime=phi(0); the assigned value at zero is immaterial.
items.statement: On R, H=1_(0,infinity) has H prime=delta_0.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Derivatives of piecewise smooth functions include jump deltas
items.strategy: Integrate by parts away from each break point, then use the finite one-sided limits and local integrability of g to pass to the endpoints. Only finitely many pieces meet a test support; C1 on open pieces alone does not guarantee that g defines a regular distribution.
items.statement: Let f be locally integrable and C1 between a locally finite set of break points, with finite one-sided values at each break point and locally integrable classical piecewise derivative g. Then Df=u_g+sum_a (f(a+)-f(a-))delta_a. In particular this applies when f is C1 up to each side of every break point.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Distributional laplacian of the newtonian kernel
items.strategy: Verify local integrability and harmonicity off zero. Apply the published Green second identity on the finite gluing obtained by removing a small closed ball from a bounding elementary region containing the test support. The test is C-infinity and the Newtonian kernel is C-infinity on a neighborhood of that punctured closure, so the supplier's two-C2 hypothesis is met. The outer boundary terms vanish; on the inner sphere track the inward normal, show the term involving the kernel times the test's normal derivative tends to zero, and compute the remaining flux limit as phi(0).
items.statement: In R^3, Delta[-1/(4 pi |x|)]=delta_0.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Principal value distribution one over x
items.strategy: Subtract phi(0) on a fixed symmetric interval around zero; the mean value bound controls the integrand, while the compact tail is integrable.
items.statement: pv(1/x)(phi)=lim_{epsilon->0} integral_|x|>epsilon phi(x)/x dx exists and is a distribution.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Not every distribution is a locally integrable function
items.strategy: If represented by f, tests off zero imply f=0 a.e. off zero, hence a.e. everywhere; then delta_0 would vanish.
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. The distribution delta_0 cannot be represented by a locally integrable function.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Pointwise convergent functions need not converge as distributions without local control
items.strategy: Take f_j(x)=j rho(jx-2) with rho supported in (-1/2,1/2), mass one. f_j(x)->0 for every x including zero, but pairing after substitution tends to phi(0).
items.statement: Pointwise convergence alone does not force distribution convergence to the same limit.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Compactly supported distributions have global finite order
items.strategy: Apply the A theorem and exhibit the direct derivative-evaluation bound; rescale cutoff monomials to exclude smaller order.
items.statement: For partial^alpha delta_a, the compact cutoff estimate has order |alpha|.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)

items.title: Sobolev weak derivatives belong to pde
items.strategy: Orientation only; this pair provides the distribution derivative definition without defining W^{k,p}.
items.statement: Sobolev spaces and weak-solution estimates are supplied by the PDE track.

references.title: Semyon Dyatlov, Lecture notes for 18.155 (2022)
